=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: _segment_credentials, the runner_before guard at line equivalent to `index - 1 > start`
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a shell command flag cluster containing `c` is immediately followed by an attached command line without whitespace, and `c` is not the last letter in the cluster, the token is one word (e.g. `-cemysql -pS3cretPass` from `bash -ce'mysql -pS3cretPass app'`). The `index - 1 > start` guard evaluates to `0 > 0` → False for this immediate-flag case, so `runner_before` is False, none of the shell-flag branches are entered, and the credential value `S3cretPass` is not masked.
  WHY: The credential scan does not parse the nested command, and the password is posted verbatim in the permission-prompt report. The spaced form `bash -ce 'mysql -pS3cretPass app'` is handled correctly (three tokens; `runner_before` is True because `index` is already 2 when `-ce` is processed). The attached form `bash -ce'mysql -pS3cretPass app'` leaks.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: lines 263, 564, 586-597, 725, 743-745
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _SHELL_COMMAND_CLUSTER_RE (r"^(-[A-Za-z]*?c)(.+)$" with re.IGNORECASE) matches single-dash multi-letter option names containing "c" or "C", such as PowerShell's -NonInteractive or -ExecutionPolicy. In _segment_shape(), when preceded by a shell runner like pwsh, such options match attached_command with attached_command.group(2).isalpha() as True (for example group(2) = "tive" or "utionPolicy"), triggering _shell_command_line_words() to consume subsequent legitimate options and script arguments (such as -File and the script path) as if they were shell -c command line values, replacing them with "*".
  WHY: command_shape() corrupts the shape of PowerShell commands containing single-dash options with "c" by dropping subsequent flags and script names (for example "pwsh -NonInteractive -File ./x.ps1" produces "pwsh -NonInteractive *"). This collapses distinct PowerShell invocations into an overly generic shape and assigns them identical pattern signatures. In addition, _segment_credentials() attempts to parse trailing option text and subsequent parameters as nested shell command lines.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: line 263 (`_SHELL_COMMAND_CLUSTER_RE = re.compile(r"^(-[A-Za-z]*?c)(.+)$", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)`); also flow in `_segment_shape` at lines 564, 586–597 and `_segment_credentials` at lines 758–771
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cluster regex `_SHELL_COMMAND_CLUSTER_RE` matches any single-dash token that contains a lowercase `c` anywhere in the word, not just short-flag clusters ending in `c`. With the non-greedy `[A-Za-z]*?c` and the unrestricted `(.+)$` suffix, the regex matches tokens such as `-NonInteractive` (group(1) = `-NonInterac`, group(2) = `tive`), `-Accept` (group(1) = `-Ac`, group(2) = `cept`), `-Continue` (group(1) = `-Continu`, group(2) = `e`), and any other single-letter flag name containing `c`. Because the matched group(2) is alphabetic, the condition at line 586 (`runner_before and (_SHELL_COMMAND_FLAG_RE.match(token) or (attached_command and attached_command.group(2).isalpha()))`) is true for any shell runner followed by a token containing `c`, and the code then calls `_shell_command_line_words(tokens, index)` to consume the following tokens as a shell "command line". For example, `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./x.ps1` would have the shape `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive * * * -File ./x.ps1` (consuming `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` as a "command line"), and `pwsh -NonInteractive -File ./x.ps1` would have the shape `pwsh -NonInteractive * * *` (consuming `-File ./x.ps1`).
  WHY: The shape is consumed by `command_shape` and posted in the `ai:permission-prompt` issue title, the `**Pattern:**` line, and the immediate-block comments. An operator reading an issue titled "Command: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive * * * -File ./x.ps1" would be confused, because `-NonInteractive * * *` looks like a shell command line. The same broken shape is also hashed into the pattern signature (`signature(...)`), so structurally different commands would get the same signature, and structurally identical commands would get different signatures, defeating the de-duplication that opens one issue per pattern. No credentials leak (the "consumed" tokens are still read as words by `_segment_credentials`, and the over-masking only affects shape), but the user-facing artefacts are corrupted for every `pwsh` / `bash` / `sh` / `su` / `runuser` invocation followed by a flag that happens to contain the letter `c` (e.g., `-NonInteractive`, `-Accept`, `-Critical`, `-Process`, `-Decrypt`, `-Receive`, etc.).
- tests/test_permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: lines 46 and 278 (both load from `TEMPLATE_SCRIPT_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "workflow-templates" / ".claude" / "scripts" / "permission_prompts.py"`); the assertion at lines 552–553
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `test_credential_free_commands_are_unchanged` asserts `pp_mask_twin.record_shape(record) == pp.record_shape(record)` and the same for `record_example`, but both `pp` (line 46) and `pp_mask_twin` (line 278) are loaded from `TEMPLATE_SCRIPT_PATH` (the workflow-templates twin). The test therefore compares the twin to itself; both modules are the same Python object (loaded from the same path with different `spec_from_file_location` names), so the assertion is always true. The new test cases added in this PR — including `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./x.ps1`, `pwsh -NoProfile -Command Get-Date`, `pwsh -Command='Get-Date'`, and the `su postgres --command='psql -c "select 1"'` family — therefore do not actually verify that the cluster regex / `-Command=` handling produces the same shape as the pre-PR implementation would, even though the test name and the comment "credential-free commands are unchanged" imply it does. The only test that would actually catch a behavioural regression against the pre-PR code is the sibling `test_template_parity` at lines 1445–1447, which reads the file contents and compares the two paths — but that only catches text-level divergence, not behavioural divergence from the same source.
  WHY: A regression in `_segment_shape` or `_segment_credentials` introduced by the cluster regex (or any other change in this PR) will not be caught by `test_credential_free_commands_are_unchanged`, because the assertion compares the module to itself. The test passes vacuously on every run, even on a broken implementation. Combined with the cluster regex issue above, this means the broken shape for `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./x.ps1` ships without any test failure.
